q: What CBAM figure does an ammonia exporter in Trinidad need for EU buyers?
title: Trinidad ammonia exporter CBAM figure
short: Ammonia (CN 2814) is a CBAM good. Its figure counts direct emissions from gas used as feed and fuel, plus indirect emissions from electricity. CO2 sent to a urea or methanol plant is usually treated as emitted unless the rules allow otherwise. Methanol itself is not a CBAM good.
audience: Ammonia and fertiliser exporters in Trinidad and Tobago

ul: Feed and fuel gas, metered and analysed.
Electricity, since indirect emissions count for fertilisers.
Any purchased hydrogen as a precursor.

p: CBAM allows a deduction only for a carbon price effectively paid in the country of origin. Check whether any applies before claiming one.
EU importers will ask for a verified actual figure per installation.

senseible: Senseible reads fuel, power and production records into dated, fingerprinted installation records, the starting point for the actual emissions your EU importer asks for.
